findings.evidence: Lines 92-96: `partner_ne : ∀ i, partner i ≠ i` and `same_iff : ∀ i j, visit i = visit j ↔ j = i ∨ j = partner i` pin every fibre to exactly two elements.
findings.fix: Drop the field and prove it as a theorem: by `same_iff`, each fibre of `visit` is `{i, D.partner i}`, of card 2 by `partner_ne`, so `2 * n = 2 * (image visit).card`, giving `(image visit).card = n = Fintype.card (Fin n)` and hence `image visit = univ`.
findings.issue: The field `visit_surjective` is implied by `same_iff` and `partner_ne`, so every constructor must reprove a consequence of the other fields.

summary: The partner data re-implements the existing `TauCeti.PerfectMatching` (fixed-point-free involution) and `CrossingSign` re-implements `ℤˣ`, Mathlib's canonical ±1 sign type; several lemmas are verbatim restatements of structure fields or of the auto-generated `ext`. Reuse the located API instead.
